summary: Snapshot 2026-10-09, 21:00 UTC. Plague is still the strongest signal on the radar. The Wikipedia "Plague (disease)" page is at 11,784 views a day and new in the top 1000, and more than 60 mainstream stories ran in 72 hours (AP, NBC, CNN, NYT, BBC, Reuters, NPR, WaPo, SciAm, Smithsonian). The news cycle has moved past "what is pneumonic plague?", which is now well covered, into new sub-stories. (1) Status change: on Oct 8 the Irkutsk governor announced that quarantine restrictions were lifted, and reported that about 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens with over 90% of contacts' monitoring complete. Credit those figures to the governor, not Rospotrebnadzor. WHO says it still lacks enough information to assess the risk, and Russian authorities called reports of a second case false. (2) Reporting rules: NPR's Oct 9 piece "Did Russia play by the rules" puts the International Health Regulations in the news. (3) An AFP Fact Check (Oct 9) on unproven plague "cures" spreading online, which is ideal for myth correction. (4) Wildlife and outdoor angles (National Geographic on marmots, Outside on US national parks, AP on plague in Africa and the US). (5) Gavi's vaccine explainer. Top picks: a dated status decoder (quarantine lifted, WHO still asking); "Plague cures online: what actually works", framed against the AFP check; "Why did quarantine end? The incubation window"; and the IHR explainer. These are at the emerging stage, and few health creators have them yet. The core search questions (person to person, symptoms, curable) are still high-demand rising staples. Every status item has to be re-checked at publish time. I flagged three candidates as reject: bioweapon/cover-up speculation, the unverified personal account of a lab accident, and permafrost fear framing.

candidates.topic: Plague case in Russia: what's confirmed vs reported (as of Oct 9, 2026). Irkutsk governor says quarantine lifted and ~5,000 tests found no dangerous pathogens; WHO says it still lacks enough information; Russian authorities call second-case reports false
candidates.angle: Dated, line-by-line decoder with each statement credited to the body that made it and the day it was made. Newest development first: quarantine lifted (governor, Oct 8). Then WHO's position: still seeking information, transparency under the IHR. Then Russia's denial of a second case. Plague is neither confirmed nor ruled out. Fits the first plague long-form and a breaking-status Short.
keywords: is the plague in russia confirmed
candidates.predicted_peak: 0–3 days (status keeps changing; refresh at every publish)
candidates.why_now: Quarantine was lifted on Oct 8, and Bloomberg, Kyiv Post and Reuters ran 'checks complete' stories on Oct 8–9. WHO is still asking Russia for details. That gap between 'over' and 'unexplained' is what people are searching for now. Our playbook says status Shorts should lead with the newest development.

candidates.topic: Plague 'cures' online: AFP Fact Check flags unproven remedies. What actually treats plague (antibiotics from clinicians, especially when started early)
candidates.angle: Myth correction with the agency named: the remedies circulating now (AFP, Oct 9) versus what CDC and WHO say actually works. No product names to amplify, no self-treatment and no stockpiling. The message is: if you're worried, contact a doctor or local health authority urgently.

candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 8 consecutive snapshots at a momentum of about 90. It is the single most-searched question, and NPR, The Naked Scientists (Oct 9) and UC Davis are all answering it. A plain question plus an agency is our best-performing title pattern.
